messages.subject: Negative variance
parts:
Hi there,

It appears that one item in my model holds a negative variance. I can't delete this item because its latent variable is only being measured by two items. 
I already tried fixing it by using other estimators than MLR...
My model appears has a good fit and my regressions are quite meaningful to me. 
If I let the residuals of those two items covariate the problem is solved, but am I aloud to do so? 
Is there any other way to fix this problem?

Thank you!

messages.author: 671b14edc9322fa7
messages.subject: Re: Negative variance
parts:
Hi

Negative error variances are typically an indication of model misspecification. This can happen if the indicator in question is correlated more highly with some other indicators than what your model implies. One way to diagnose the issue further is to fix the error to a plausible non-sero value (e.g. 30% of its total variance) and then diagnose the fit of that model.

You should generally not allow the indicator error terms to correlate. A latent variable can be interpreted as the shared variance of its indicators. If you free the error correlation, you can no longer make this interpretation and it would be very difficult to interpret what the latent variable means.

Using a different estimator is unlikely to help.

Mikko

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Negative variance
parts:
With only two indicators for the factor, it is a bit surprising that the model with free residual Covariance is statistically identified.  If you want that parameter to be free and nonzero, you would need to think carefully about what the factor represents--what covariance it actually accounts for.
     Sometimes--maybe most times--negative residual variances point to a problem with the model, where, even if fit indices look good, the empirical covariance matrix just does not match well with the factor model.  But it is also possible that, if the population value of a residual covariance is positive but near zero, a particular sample based estimate could be negative, just like any random variable with a mean near 0.

Kolenikov and Bollen (2012) in Sociological Methods and Research offer one take on diagnosing Negative residual variances.  Chen, Bollen et al (2001) in the same journal present the argument for negative residual variances as being due to sampling variance.
--Ed Rigdon
